prompt.en: A simple three-element Yagi points from left to right. The feedline is on the centre element. Which order fits its RF roles, from rear to front?

text.en: Short director, fed driven element, long reflector.

feedback.en: This reverses the main direction: the shorter director belongs at the front, not behind the fed element.

text.en: Long reflector, fed driven element, short director.

feedback.en: The longer reflector is behind the fed driven element; the shorter director is forward.

text.en: Fed driven element, long reflector, short director.

feedback.en: The description puts the feedline on the centre element, so the driven element cannot be the rear element here.

text.en: Long director, fed driven element, short reflector.

feedback.en: The terminal names and lengths are reversed. In this simple Yagi, the reflector is longer and the director shorter.

explanation.en: A simple Yagi directs its main beam toward the shorter director. The fed driven element lies between that director and the longer rear reflector.

prompt.en: A nearby signal remains audible beside a wanted CW signal even though AGC keeps loudness steady. Which change most directly improves separation?

text.en: Set a faster AGC response while keeping the same passband.

feedback.en: AGC manages gain as strength varies. It does not narrow the frequency range reaching the detector.

text.en: Raise audio volume while keeping both signals in the passband.

feedback.en: Audio volume raises what is already present, including the interfering signal. It does not separate the frequencies.

text.en: Use a wider IF filter to give the detector more signal.

feedback.en: A wider filter admits more nearby spectrum. It is the opposite of the needed selectivity change.

text.en: Use a narrower filter that still passes the wanted CW signal.

feedback.en: Suitable filter width rejects nearby frequencies while retaining the wanted signal. AGC and selectivity do different jobs.

explanation.en: AGC regulates level as strength changes. Selectivity determines which nearby frequencies pass through to detection.

prompt.en: A waterfall shows two close traces. The receiver audio blends them into a rough sound. Which next step best uses that display?

text.en: Tune to the wanted trace and select a filter narrow enough to separate it.

feedback.en: The display locates the signals. Tuning and suitable selectivity determine which reaches the recovered audio.

text.en: Lower display contrast until the weaker trace fades, keeping the audio passband.

feedback.en: Display contrast changes what you see. It does not narrow the receive passband.

text.en: Tune halfway between the traces, keeping both inside a wide passband.

feedback.en: Keeping both signals inside the passband still sends both to the detector. Centre on the wanted one with suitable filtering.

text.en: Reduce AF gain until the unwanted trace is quiet, keeping both inside the passband.

feedback.en: AF gain changes audio level after reception. It lowers both signals instead of separating their frequencies.

explanation.en: The waterfall helps locate signals, while receive tuning and filter width determine which of them become audio.
